hints.content:
The [[☃ definition 1]] is in the form $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{p(x)}}$ where $p(x)$ is a quadratic expression. This suggests that we should rewrite $p(x)$ by completing the square.

Specifically, we will rewrite $p(x)$ as $\maroonD k^2-(x+\blueD h)^2$. Then, we will be able to integrate using our knowledge of the derivative of the inverse sine function:

$\displaystyle\int \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\maroonD k^2-x^2}}\,dx=\text{arcsin}\left(\dfrac{x}{\maroonD k}\right)+C$

[[☃ explanation 1]]

By setting $u=x+\blueD h$ and using $u$-substitution, we get the following formula:

$\displaystyle\int \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\maroonD k^2-(x+\blueD h)^2}}\,dx=\text{arcsin}\left(\dfrac{x+\blueD h}{\maroonD k}\right)+C$

options.definition: The integrand is the expression within the integral expression. For example, the integrand of $\displaystyle\int (5x+1)\,dx$ is $5x+1$.

options.explanation:
This is the formula for the derivative of $\text{arcsin}(x)$:

$\dfrac{d}{dx}\text{arcsin}(x)=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$

Let's differentiate $\text{arcsin}\left(\dfrac{x}{\maroonD k}\right)$:

$\begin{align}
&\phantom{=}\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\text{arcsin}\left(\dfrac{x}{\maroonD k}\right)\right]
\\\\
&=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-\left(\dfrac{x}{\maroonD k}\right)^2}}\cdot\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\dfrac{x}{\maroonD k}\right]
\\\\
&=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\dfrac{\maroonD{k}^2-x^2}{\maroonD k^2}}}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\maroonD{k}}
\\\\
&=\dfrac{\sqrt{\maroonD k^2}}{\sqrt{\maroonD k^2-x^2}}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\maroonD{k}}
\\\\
&=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\maroonD k^2-x^2}}
\end{align}$

Now we can reverse the order to find the indefinite integral of $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\maroonD k^2-x^2}}$:

$\displaystyle\int \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\maroonD k^2-x^2}}\,dx=\text{arcsin}\left(\dfrac{x}{\maroonD k}\right)+C$

hints.content:
We start by rewriting $p(x)$ as $\maroonD k^2-(x+\blueD h)^2$:

$\begin{align}
-x^2+10x+11&=11-(x^2-10x)
\\\\
&=11+25-(x^2-10x+25)
\\\\
&=36-(x-5)^2
\\\\
&=\maroonD{6}^2-(x\blueD{-5})^2
\end{align}$

Now we can find the integral:

$\begin{align}
&\phantom{=}\displaystyle\int \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{-x^2+10x+11}}\,dx
\\\\
&=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\maroonD{6}^2-(x\blueD{-5})^2}}\,dx
\\\\
&=\text{arcsin}\left(\dfrac{x\blueD{-5}}{\maroonD{6}}\right)+C
\end{align}$
